analysis_summary: Validated eight Phase 1 and semgrep candidates across public REST routes, AJAX handlers, admin bootstrap paths, settings saves, and connection flows. No Patchstack-eligible source-to-sink vulnerability survived refutation. One real but low-impact open redirect exists in the privileged wc_fbe_redirect flow; it requires manage_woocommerce and only appends non-secret onboarding metadata, so it is tracked as out of scope.

negative_findings.title: Public /fb_api/offers registration is backed by Meta-signed JWT validation and catalog binding

reasoning.hypothesis: permission_callback = __return_true on /fb_api/offers might expose coupon create, read, and delete operations to unauthenticated callers.
reasoning.trace: The route is registered publicly at OfferManagementEndpointBase.php:84-90, but execute_with_validation() refuses requests unless feature flags are enabled, jwt_params is present, RequestVerification::decode_jwt_with_retries() accepts the token, and the decoded aud claim matches the configured catalog ID before execute_endpoint() is reached.
reasoning.defenses: RequestVerification selects Meta public keys by project, retries with refreshed keys when needed, and JWTCodec::decode() verifies algorithm, ECDSA signature, and exp before returning claims.
reasoning.refutation: I traced the only privileged sinks reachable from this route to coupon creation at CreateOffersEndpoint.php:29-34 and coupon deletion at DeleteOffersEndpoint.php:27-35. Both stay behind the JWT and catalog checks in OfferManagementEndpointBase.php:128-145, so the Phase 1 'public REST' signal does not produce an unauthenticated exploit path on its own.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as a false positive. The route is intentionally public at the WordPress layer, but it implements an application-layer trust boundary using Meta-signed JWTs and store-specific catalog binding.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show a practical way for an attacker without Meta's signing key to forge a token accepted by RequestVerification, or a reachable code path that invokes execute_endpoint() before the JWT and aud checks.

negative_findings.title: wc_facebook_dismiss_notice only mutates the caller's own user meta

reasoning.hypothesis: The AJAX dismiss handler lacks current_user_can() and might let lower-privileged users perform an admin-only action.
reasoning.trace: The handler checks a per-action nonce at facebook-commerce-admin-notice.php:52-53 and then writes update_user_meta(get_current_user_id(), self::NOTICE_ID, 1) at line 54.
reasoning.defenses: The sink is hard-coded to the current session user. No user_id, option key, or capability-controlled object can be chosen by the caller.
reasoning.refutation: Even if another logged-in user can hit wp_ajax_wc_facebook_dismiss_notice, the only effect is dismissing this notice for that same account. I found no path to alter another user's state or any site-wide setting.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as a false positive because the missing capability check does not create measurable security impact.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show a code path where the handler can target another user or mutate shared/plugin-wide state.

negative_findings.title: Product and feed sync AJAX handlers are protected by manage_woocommerce and action-specific nonces

reasoning.hypothesis: Phase 1 classified several wp_ajax_* sync endpoints as subscriber-reachable and potentially capable of triggering catalog sync actions.
reasoning.trace: Each sync/status entry point immediately calls WC_Facebookcommerce_Utils::is_legit_ajax_call() before any privileged action: sync_products() at AJAX.php:109-121, sync_coupons() at 134-140, sync_shipping_profiles() at 153-159, sync_navigation_menu() at 172-179, and get_sync_status() at 192-216.
reasoning.defenses: is_legit_ajax_call() is defined in fbutils.php:502-503 as current_user_can('manage_woocommerce') && check_ajax_referer($action, $nonce).
reasoning.refutation: Because check_ajax_referer() aborts on failure and manage_woocommerce is checked first, I could not trace any subscriber or unauthenticated path into the sync sinks.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as a false positive. These endpoints are not exploitable by subscriber-level users despite the coarse IR auth heuristic.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show a call site that exposes one of these nonces to a lower-privileged role or a code path where is_legit_ajax_call() is bypassed.

negative_findings.title: PluginRender nopriv AJAX hooks still require a manage_woocommerce session plus nonce

reasoning.hypothesis: The presence of wp_ajax_nopriv_* hooks in PluginRender might let anonymous users toggle sync behavior or banner state.
reasoning.trace: The nopriv hooks are registered at PluginRender.php:86-95, but every state-changing callback immediately gates on is_legit_ajax_call(): opt_out_of_sync_clicked() at 205-212, sync_all_clicked() at 215-221, product_set_banner_closed() at 224-229, and both banner-reset methods at 236-266.
reasoning.defenses: is_legit_ajax_call() requires current_user_can('manage_woocommerce') and a valid action nonce, so anonymous requests fail before any option or transient write.
reasoning.refutation: I traced the supposedly dangerous sinks update_option(self::MASTER_SYNC_OPT_OUT_TIME, ...) and set_transient(...) and found no path from the nopriv registration to those sinks without the manage_woocommerce guard succeeding.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as a false positive. The nopriv registrations are noisy, but they do not create an anonymous state-change primitive.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show any PluginRender callback reachable from a nopriv hook that does not call is_legit_ajax_call() first.

negative_findings.title: Settings, WhatsApp, extras, and webhook REST routes do define manage_woocommerce permission callbacks

reasoning.hypothesis: Semgrep reported several wc-facebook/v1 routes as missing permission callbacks or being effectively public.
reasoning.trace: Settings routes register permission_callback => [ $this, 'permission_callback' ] at Settings/Handler.php:35-52, WhatsApp routes do the same at WhatsAppSettings/Handler.php:35-63, the extras route uses extras_permission_callback at Connection.php:1463-1470 and 1484-1485, and the webhook route uses permission_callback at WebHook.php:41-48 and 63-64.
reasoning.defenses: The shared AbstractRESTEndpoint::permission_callback() returns current_user_can('manage_woocommerce') at AbstractRESTEndpoint.php:40-41; Connection::extras_permission_callback() and WebHook::permission_callback() do the same explicitly.
reasoning.refutation: I verified the source rather than relying on the static rule messages. These routes are not missing permission callbacks in the shipped code.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as false positives caused by rule overmatching or stale assumptions.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show a concrete wc-facebook/v1 route in this plugin that reaches a sensitive callback without any permission_callback check.

negative_findings.title: is_admin() is used for admin bootstrap and migration, not as the sole authorization check for writes

reasoning.hypothesis: Phase 1 and semgrep flagged is_admin() usage as broken access control because subscribers can reach wp-admin/admin-ajax.php.
reasoning.trace: The flagged branches at class-wc-facebookcommerce.php:259-267 and facebook-commerce.php:315-388 and 455-479 are bootstrap/migration logic that instantiate admin handlers, enqueue admin assets, or synchronize pixel settings. The state-changing save paths later enforce capability and nonces: Settings::save() at Settings.php:249-263 and Enhanced_Settings::save() at Enhanced_Settings.php:265-283.
reasoning.defenses: Both save handlers require Helper::get_requested_value('page') === 'wc-facebook', current_user_can('manage_woocommerce'), and check_admin_referer(...).
reasoning.refutation: I did not find a write sink reachable only because is_admin() evaluated true. The actual sinks remain guarded inside the invoked admin handlers.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as a false positive. The is_admin() calls are not the final authorization boundary in the reviewed flows.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show a concrete state-changing method inside one of these bootstrap branches that executes without its own capability or nonce checks.

negative_findings.title: Flagged option updates write fixed plugin keys after guarded validation, not attacker-chosen option names

reasoning.hypothesis: Semgrep reported arbitrary option update style privilege escalation in Product_Attributes and Connection/API settings handlers.
reasoning.trace: Product_Attributes::process_form_submission() first validates save_attribute_mappings_nonce at lines 892-894, sanitizes posted arrays at 903-904, whitelists only existing attribute keys at 906-918, and writes only the fixed option self::OPTION_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPINGS at line 939. The REST settings handlers similarly map request fields to hard-coded plugin option constants rather than attacker-controlled keys.
reasoning.defenses: There is no user-controlled option name. The writable keys are fixed constants in plugin code, and the REST handlers sit behind manage_woocommerce permission callbacks while the admin form uses a dedicated nonce.
reasoning.refutation: I could not build a path from user input to update_option($arbitrary_key, ...) or to security-sensitive core options like users_can_register/default_role.
reasoning.conclusion: Rejected as a false positive. The flagged sinks are fixed plugin setting writes, not arbitrary option update primitives.
reasoning.reopen_if: Show a path where request data controls the option name passed to update_option(), or where one of these handlers can write a security-sensitive core option.

reasoning.hypothesis: The App Store login redirect flow may allow a privileged user to supply an external redirect target.
reasoning.trace: handle_fbe_redirect() base64-decodes $_REQUEST['redirect_uri'] at Connection.php:1514, validates it with preg_match('/https?:\/\/(www\.|m\.|l\.)?(\d{5}\.od\.)?(facebook|instagram|whatsapp)\.com(\/.*)?/') at line 1516, then forwards it to wp_redirect($redirect_url) at line 1533. Because the regex is not anchored to the end of the string, values such as https://facebook.com@evil.com/path and https://facebook.com.evil.com still satisfy the check.
reasoning.defenses: The flow requires current_user_can('manage_woocommerce') at lines 1511-1512. On the success branch it appends only get_connect_parameters_extras(), which contains onboarding metadata such as external_business_id, timezone, currency, domain, and business name at Connection.php:1100-1122, not access tokens.
reasoning.refutation: I validated the regex behavior separately and confirmed it matches attacker-controlled hosts that merely begin with a facebook.com or instagram.com prefix. parse_url('https://facebook.com@evil.com/path') resolves host = evil.com, so the redirect can leave the intended allowlist.
reasoning.conclusion: This is a real open redirect, but it is low severity and not Patchstack-eligible in this context because exploitation already requires a privileged manage_woocommerce account and does not expose secret tokens in the reviewed code path.

out_of_scope.poc_description: Log in as a Shop Manager or Administrator and browse to /?wc-api=wc_fbe_redirect&success=1&redirect_uri=<base64 of https://facebook.com@evil.com/path>. The regex allowlist accepts the value and wp_redirect() sends the browser to evil.com with an extras= JSON blob appended.
out_of_scope.remediation: Parse the decoded URL and compare the normalized host exactly against an allowlist of expected domains, or replace the regex with strict host validation and wp_safe_redirect().
